preparation: Provide the actual official world political map and its key in a digital view and a printed copy. Select the Canada country label, Ottawa national-capital key example and another labelled populated place.

Provide a small original transfer map whose key explicitly uses a different font/symbol scheme for verified country/capital/place labels; label it as a teaching representation, not a new official map.
performance: Identify the kind of entity represented by each selected label using the actual key, typography and known place context. Explain how the visual style communicates the distinction.
Compare the printed and digital representations; explain that a style is a map convention, not a fact that every uppercase label in every map must mean one entity type.
Use the different keyed teaching map to apply the convention rather than carry over a single font rule.
protocols.positive: Correctly decodes selected entity types in both media and explains how the supplied map convention signals the difference.
protocols.nearMiss: Reads the words but ignores the key, or declares that every bold/uppercase label is the same type in every map.

preparation: Choose the main Ontario reference map, retaining its scale and a geographic extent suitable for the selected public places. Prepare the digital base and a print version without changing the base-to-bar relationship.

Verify the selected city/community points from the actual map and Nation’s own account. Use North Bay, Niagara Falls and the attributed Nipissing First Nation public community/administration reference; distinguish community point, reserve outline and traditional territory.
Supply any location information needed for plotting and an accurate graphic scale in kilometres. Do not import legal survey work, a new app/account or formal ratio-redrawing demands.
performance: Construct an original paper map or a digital map over the supplied reference base, using selected labelled Ontario city/community locations including the First Nation example, a title and a clear symbol key.

Retain the correct supplied metric scale with the map. Explain what its kilometre units mean and use repeated equal graphic-bar units to compare an appropriate approximate distance; precision must match the small-scale map.
Explain why a reserve/background reference is not a map of every traditional territory, and why changing the map size requires keeping the graphic bar with it.
protocols.positive: Produces a coherent selected-place map with the First Nation reference and correct labels/key/metric reference, then explains and uses its units without borrowing the inset scale.
protocols.nearMiss: Copies an unrelated scale, labels centimetres on paper as ground kilometres with no given relationship, substitutes a reserve for all traditional territory or invents precise legal boundaries.
protocols.contributor: mt_w4cUnN_SsQ supplies map construction/key/labels; appropriate existing length-measurement and equal-unit comparison operations support the graphic-unit task. Broader formal scale-drawing and rescaling mastery is not inferred.
